Construct fbswicd objects from summary data frames

Source: R/as_fbswicd.R
as_fbswicd.Rd

as_fbswicd() constructs the summary-level object used by create_asr(), create_quality(), and related functions. Supply one summarized incidence table and its matching population table. Optional site/morphology frequencies and excluded records can also be included.

Usage

as_fbswicd(
  fbsw,
  pop,
  sitemorp = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  regicode = NULL,
  regicode_var = NULL
)

Arguments

fbsw

A data frame with the key columns year, sex, cancer, and agegrp, plus the required incidence count fbs. Optional count columns sws, mv, dco, mvs, ub, sub, ids, and mult are retained when supplied.

pop

A population data frame with year, sex, agegrp, and rks. An optional death column is retained.

sitemorp

Optional data frame with year, sex, cancer, icd10, and morp. The last two columns must be list-columns of named numeric frequency vectors.

exclude

Optional data frame containing records excluded during case cleaning. Its columns are retained without imposing a case schema.

regicode

One non-missing registry identifier. It must be NULL when regicode_var is supplied.

regicode_var

Optional name of a registry-code column. When supplied, fbsw and pop must contain exactly the same codes. Optional components may contain a subset of those codes. The grouping column is removed from constructed components.

Value

One object of class fbswicd, or a named fbswicds object when regicode_var contains multiple registry codes. A single code still returns one fbswicd object.

Details

Count columns may be numeric or numeric text. They are converted to numeric values and must be finite and non-negative. Population denominators cannot be missing; missing optional death counts are preserved. Omitted optional count columns are not filled with zeros. When sitemorp or exclude is NULL, that component is omitted. An explicitly supplied zero-row data frame is retained, distinguishing an available empty component from one that was not supplied. Rate and quality functions interpret absent age rows within an observed summary year/sex/cancer stratum as zero counts, using matching population ages. Entirely absent strata and missing population rows are not inferred. Registry order follows first appearance in fbsw. Functions calculating mortality or quality indicators still require their corresponding count columns.

Examples

data("canregs")
counted <- count_canreg(canregs[[1]])
rebuilt <- as_fbswicd(
  fbsw = counted$fbswicd,
  pop = counted$pop,
  sitemorp = counted$sitemorp,
  exclude = counted$exclude,
  regicode = counted$regicode
)
